questions.q: What does the small icon next to each field in the Data pane represent?
options: The field's data type (string, number, date, geographic, boolean)
Whether the field is used in the current worksheet
The field's default color in every chart
Whether the field came from a Live connection or an Extract
questions.explain: Each field icon (Abc, #, calendar, globe, T/F) indicates its data type, which drives what you can do with it in the view.

questions.q: How do you fix a field whose data type Tableau guessed incorrectly (e.g., a ZIP code read as a number)?
options: Right-click the field and choose Change Data Type
Edit the original source file directly — Tableau has no way to override it
Delete the field and recreate the entire data source
This can only be fixed using a calculated field
questions.explain: Change Data Type corrects how Tableau interprets a field without altering the underlying source file.

options: The aggregation (SUM, AVG, etc.) Tableau automatically applies whenever a Measure is dragged into a view
The default chart type Show Me picks for a field
A setting that only applies to Dimensions, never Measures
The order fields appear in the Data pane
questions.explain: Default Aggregation determines what happens automatically when a Measure is used — most numeric fields default to SUM, but this can be changed per field.

questions.q: Why would you set a field's default number format (e.g., currency on Sales) once at the field level rather than per worksheet?
options: Because every worksheet that uses that field afterward automatically inherits the format, saving repeated manual formatting
Because Tableau requires it before the field can be used at all
Because per-worksheet formatting is not supported in Tableau
It has no practical benefit over setting it per worksheet
questions.explain: Field-level defaults (aggregation, number format, comment, color) are inherited by every future worksheet that uses the field, avoiding repeated manual setup.

questions.q: What is a practical example of when you'd change a Measure's default aggregation away from SUM?
options: A percentage or satisfaction-score field, which usually makes more sense defaulting to Average
Sales, which should always default to Count instead of Sum
Any field that is a Dimension, since Dimensions default to Sum
Never — default aggregation cannot be changed
questions.explain: A field like Profit Ratio or a satisfaction score is more meaningful averaged than summed, so changing its default aggregation to AVG avoids repeatedly fixing it by hand.
